uncited: Grid Partitioning by Cell Size converts a point cloud into a regular 3D voxel grid by partitioning the spatial extent defined by the cloud's bounding box or a user-specified origin into uniform cubic cells.
It solves the problem of discretizing continuous point data into a structured volume representation for downstream rendering or analysis.

It differs from [Octree Construction for Point Clouds](1070-octree-construction-for-point-clouds.md) by using a fixed-resolution regular grid rather than an adaptive hierarchical structure, and from [Point Resampling with Neighbor Masking](2710-point-resampling-with-neighbor-masking.md) by not explicitly handling neighbor interactions during the initial partitioning step.
All variants in this family share the core mechanism of mapping 3D coordinates $(x, y, z)$ to integer voxel indices $(v_x, v_y, v_z)$ using a fixed spacing $s$ (cell length).
where $p_i$ is the point coordinate, $o_i$ is the grid origin, and $s$ is the cell size along axis $i$.
The resulting indices are clamped or checked against the grid dimensions $D_x, D_y, D_z$.
The output is typically a binary mask or a data array associated with the grid geometry.
A voxelization mode that uses a pre-existing destination grid geometry.
